:::{#def-jacobian-matrix}
#### Jacobian matrix

Let $\vy = \vy(\vb) = \tp{(y_1, \ldots, y_q)}$ be a $q \times 1$ vector-valued function
of the $p \times 1$ vector $\vb$.
The **Jacobian matrix** of $\vy$ is the $q \times p$ matrix
whose $(j, i)$ entry is $\deriv{\beta_i} y_j$,
for $j = 1, \ldots, q$ and $i = 1, \ldots, p$.
It is the transpose of the derivative $\deriv{\vb} \tp{\vy}$ of @def-vector-valued-derivative.
Writing derivatives this way,
with rows indexing the entries of $\vy$ (the numerator)
and columns indexing the entries of $\vb$ (the denominator),
is the **numerator layout**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-jacobian-matrix}
#### The Jacobian matrix of a $3 \times 1$ function of a $2 \times 1$ vector

For $\vy(\vb) = \tp{(\beta_1^2,\ \beta_1\beta_2,\ 3\beta_2)}$ of @exm-vector-valued-derivative,
the Jacobian matrix is the $3 \times 2$ matrix

$$
\sbmat{
\deriv{\beta_1} \beta_1^2 & \deriv{\beta_2} \beta_1^2 \\
\deriv{\beta_1} \beta_1\beta_2 & \deriv{\beta_2} \beta_1\beta_2 \\
\deriv{\beta_1} 3\beta_2 & \deriv{\beta_2} 3\beta_2
}
= \sbmat{
2\beta_1 & 0 \\
\beta_2 & \beta_1 \\
0 & 3
},
$$

the transpose of the $2 \times 3$ matrix found there.

:::
